answer: I'd like to describe a present I made for someone rather than bought, because it is the one I'm proudest of. A gift I was particularly pleased with was a photo album I put together for my mother's birthday. My mother has spent her whole life looking after all of us, and I felt she deserved something that celebrated that. Rather than buying something generic, I wanted to give her something genuinely [[meaningful]]. I chose an album because I knew she would never ask for anything for herself, and memories matter far more to her than possessions. I spent weeks gathering old family photographs and arranging them chronologically, adding little notes beside each one. Some of them I found in a dusty trunk at my grandparents' village home, including a faded picture of her wedding day, and my elder sister secretly sent me a few from Dhaka as well. It was surprisingly time-consuming, but the effort felt worthwhile. When she opened it, her reaction was absolutely [[priceless]]; she was moved to tears as she flicked through the memories. She kept stopping at certain pages to tell us the story behind each picture, and we ended up sitting around the dining table for hours. What made it so special was that it cost very little money but a great deal of care. She told me it was the most [[heartfelt]] gift she had ever received, which [[meant the world to me]]. Honestly, seeing her so [[delighted]] was far more rewarding than giving an expensive present ever could be. That experience confirmed my belief that the best gifts are personal ones that show you truly know the person. It is something she still treasures and shows to visitors.

followUps.q: Do you enjoy choosing gifts for people?
followUps.answer: Yes, very much, although it takes me a long time. I like noticing what people mention in passing, so that the gift feels [[personalised]] rather than something picked up at the last minute.

followUps.q: Would you make a homemade gift again?
followUps.answer: Definitely. I'm actually planning one for my grandparents, a small booklet of old family stories and photos, because I think they would value that far more than anything from a shop.
